Once upon a time there were four little rabbits, and their names were Flopsy, Mopsy, Cotton-tail and Peter.
They lived with their mum, Mrs. Rabbit, in a cosy little burrow under a big fir tree.
Peter was the littlest one.
He had a brand-new green jacket and two little red shoes.
Mrs. Rabbit gave his cheek a little pat.
One morning Mrs. Rabbit picked up her basket.
I'm off to the shops,
said Mrs. Rabbit.
You can play in the field, or go and pick blackberries down the lane.
But stay out of Mr. McGregor's garden!
It's his garden, not ours.
Okay?
As soon as Mum was gone, off ran Flopsy, Mopsy and Cotton-tail down the lane to pick blackberries.
But Peter didn't go with them.
He wanted yummy vegetables!
So he hopped the other way, straight to Mr. McGregor's garden.
Lippity, lippity, lippity!
Mr. McGregor's garden had a big green gate, with a little gap at the bottom.
Peter squeezed under it.
Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle!
Up on the gate post, two little sparrows shook their heads.
But Peter didn't look back.
The garden was full of yummy things.
Munch, munch, munch!
First Peter ate some lettuce.
Then he ate some crunchy beans.
And then he ate some radishes, one, two, three!
Yum, yum, yum!
said Peter.
Uh-oh!
Soon Peter's tummy felt very, very full, and a bit funny.
Ooh, my tummy,
I ate way too much!
He was so hot!
So he hung his jacket on a bean pole and put his shoes down next to it.
Then he lay down for a little rest in the cool shade of a big rhubarb leaf.
After his rest, Peter hopped off to find the gate.
He forgot his jacket and shoes!
But the bean plants were taller than Peter, and every path looked the same.
Which way is the gate?
A little mouse ran by with a big pea in her mouth.
She couldn't say a word, so she just shook her head.
Peter sat down next to a watering can.
He felt very small, and a little bit lost.
Then he remembered what Mum said that morning.
Oh dear,
I should've listened to my mum.
Creak, creak, creak!
Along the path came Mr. McGregor with his wheelbarrow.
Who's been nibbling my lettuces?
said Mr. McGregor.
Grumble, grumble, grumble!
Peter hid behind a big cabbage and stayed as still as a stone.
By the bean poles, Mr. McGregor found a little green jacket and two little red shoes.
Well, well, well!
Just the right size for my scarecrow!
So he dressed up his scarecrow in them.
And for the first time all day, Mr. McGregor smiled.
When Mr. McGregor went in for his lunch, a robin with a round red tummy hopped down next to Peter.
Please, can you help me find the gate?
Tweet, tweet, tweet!
said Robin.
Of course I can!
Follow me.
I know the way!
Robin flew from bush to bush, and Peter hopped along behind him.
They went past the carrots, past the onions, and past the scarecrow in its little green jacket.
But the scarecrow was much too tall, and Peter was much too small.
Bye-bye, jacket! Bye-bye, shoes!
And there it was, the big green gate!
Thank you, Robin!
Now hop straight home!
said Robin, and he waved his wing.
Peter hopped all the way home to the big fir tree.
Mrs. Rabbit gave him a great big hug.
Peter! Where are your jacket and shoes?
I went into Mr. McGregor's garden,
I'm really sorry, Mum.
Next time, I'll listen.
I promise!
Peter's tummy still felt funny, so Mrs. Rabbit tucked him into bed with a little cup of camomile tea.
Flopsy, Mopsy and Cotton-tail had bread and milk and blackberries for supper.
We saved you some blackberries for tomorrow, Peter,
said Flopsy.
Night-night, my little bunnies,
And soon Peter was fast asleep.
